label: winner or champion of
definition: X won the competition or award designated by Y, or held its championship title.
scope_notes: The win/champion/winner dictionary includes sports and honor-award uses. Explicit titles designated by sanctioning bodies qualify. Participation, qualifying, reaching an event and event-stage victory without overall title alone do not. Historical wins count.

facts.reason: Cubs win the World Series in direct and relative-clause paths. Participation and appearance rows are mixed but do not erase textual win support.
Lewis is World Boxing Council champion and holds or retains its designated title and crown, within the explicitly broad title scope.
Patriots win the Super Bowl and are its champions; losses or appearances can concern separate events.

Winning the White House denotes political office, while presence, movement and spokesman rows add other meanings. The declared predicate concerns competition titles and honors, not political officeholding.
Becker is explicitly Wimbledon champion and wins Wimbledon. A later final loss and preparation rows do not negate historical title evidence.
